newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev recovers at close with c bank help.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev recovers at close with c bank help.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 229-230 per dollar, stronger than the morning's 235-236 levels, due to central bank dollar sales, dealers said.
"For the first time in several weeks the lev closed firmer, which today was due to the active support from the central bank," a dealer said.
The lev was also higher than at Thursday's close of 234-235 to the dollar, the dealer added.

Interbank trade started in low volume near 235 levs per dollar, but a rise in clients' foreign currency demand on the illiquid market instantly pressured the lev to 237.50-238 per dollar around midday, dealers said.
The central bank then stepped in, offering relatively large dollar volumes initially at 232 levs per dollar and then at 229-230, dealers said.
According to some traders, the central bank sold dollars to several banks in volumes between $200,000 and $300,000 per bank to cover demand.
Central bank officials declined comment. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
